name: Stavanger Airport, Sola
before:
Norway's third busiest airport, 11 km south west of central Stavanger in Sola municipality, and the regional hub for the south west of the country.

What makes it unusual is the helicopters. Alongside normal airline traffic, two helicopter companies fly from here to the offshore oil installations in the North Sea, and the Royal Norwegian Air Force operates search and rescue helicopters from Sola Air Station on the same site.

Four airlines fly to four domestic destinations and eleven airlines to 35 international ones. The busiest route by far is Stavanger to Oslo Gardermoen, with around 28 flights a day.

There is an aeronautical museum, Flyhistorisk Museum Sola, in the vicinity.

The airport is commonly called Sola, after the municipality, so both names turn up in supplier systems.
after:
Norway's fourth busiest airport, 11 km south west of central Stavanger in Sola municipality.

What makes it unusual is the helicopters. Alongside the airlines, Bristow and CHC fly offshore workers from a separate helicopter terminal to the oil installations in the North Sea, and the Royal Norwegian Air Force flies search and rescue helicopters from its base on the military side of the airport.

Its full name is Stavanger Airport, Sola. Many people call it just Sola, so expect to see both names.
